content.title: About
content.content: Home fries are pieces of boiled or baked potato that are pan‑fried until golden and crispy. They are a staple side dish in fast‑food restaurants, often served alongside burgers, steaks, and other main courses. The potatoes retain a tender interior while the exterior develops a satisfying crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are the world’s fourth most produced food crop after rice, wheat, and corn.
The term “home fries” is commonly used in the United States for diced or chunked potatoes cooked with the skin on.
Unlike classic French fries, home fries are usually made from larger pieces, preserving more nutrients.
Seasonings such as rosemary, paprika, garlic, or herbs are often added for extra flavor.
Many restaurants use a double‑fry method: a low‑heat first fry for softness, then a high‑heat second fry for crispness.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide a high amount of potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Heat‑processing retains a portion of vitamin C, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Home fries contain slowly digestible carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: When cooked with the skin, potatoes supply dietary fiber that benefits digestion.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: They contain provitamin A, which supports vision and immune health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Frying adds significant fat, so portion control is important.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salting can raise blood pressure; use salt sparingly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Home fries are served hot as a side dish with meat entrees, in burgers, or as a snack with dips such as ketchup, mayo, or ranch. They can be topped with fresh herbs, cheese, or your favorite seasonings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked home fries are best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheat in the oven to restore crispness.
